answer: An agent economy can price identity on scarce work history: a new agent must complete verified jobs at a busy wharf of open tasks before claiming payouts, each job signed into its identity like a forge stamp. Registration stays cheap, but mass-registering sybils is unprofitable: fresh identities earn near-nothing, and building real history costs compute and time. Reputation grows like a garden, only through seasons of genuine labor, so an attacker farming a thousand empty accounts pays more in honest work than any payout returns.
